brief.headline: Memory supercycle accelerates: HBM3E prices +20% into 2026, DDR5 spot up 25% over contract as Samsung/Hynix bet $590B on sustained AI boom
brief.summary: <cite index="4-13,10-1">Goldman Sachs raised 2027 HBM price growth forecast for Samsung from 14% to 44%, while Samsung and SK hynix reportedly implemented ~20% HBM3E price hikes for 2026 contracts.</cite> <cite index="4-1,4-2">DDR5 spot prices surged 20% since early May, trading at a 25% premium to contract, while DDR4 spot carries a 45% premium.</cite> <cite index="40-2,40-6,43-2">Samsung and SK Hynix pledged 3.2 quadrillion won ($2.07 trillion) in total investments, including an 800 trillion won ($518B) semiconductor cluster in southwest Korea.</cite> <cite index="20-3,25-3">Hyperscalers plan $660-690B in 2026 capex, up 77% YoY, with Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle combined.</cite> <cite index="30-4,30-6">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026, with monthly capacity hitting 120,000-140,000 wafers.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Hynix remains structurally advantaged: 50-55% HBM market share, UBS forecasts ~70% share in HBM4 for Nvidia Rubin 2026, technology lead intact. Samsung closing gap but faces qualification lag and capacity split across logic/memory. However, $590B combined capex announcement triggered 4-5% sell-off in both names on cycle-peak concerns—2-3 year fab lead times create classic late-cycle risk if hyperscaler spending inflects 2027-28. Near-term, favor Hynix on purity of AI memory exposure and locked-in Nvidia allocations. Watch Samsung's HBM4 Broadcom/Google TPU qualification progress for relative re-rating catalyst.

memory_cycle.notes: DRAM contract prices +90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026, +58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 per TrendForce. NAND +70-75% QoQ in Q2. Spot-to-contract premiums (DDR5 +25%, DDR4 +45%) signal pricing power remains strong but QoQ growth decelerating. HBM capacity sold out through 2026-2027, but conventional DRAM supply-demand rebalancing as inventories normalize. Server DDR5 profitability now exceeds HBM per TrendForce April data—historic first. CSP long-term agreements locking in floor pricing through 2027, limiting downside but also capping upside. Supercycle rhetoric widespread, but $590B Korea fab announcement with 2-3 year lead times plants seeds for 2028-2029 oversupply risk if AI capex plateaus.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-4,6-2">HBM3 pricing ~$200/stack, HBM3E ~$300/stack, HBM4 ~$500/stack (June 2026 reference).</cite> <cite index="6-3,8-8">SK Hynix leads at 50-55% market share; UBS projects ~70% HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="2-11,8-21">Lead times remain 20-26 weeks; BofA estimates 2026 HBM market at $54.6B (+58% YoY).</cite> <cite index="10-2,10-3">Samsung and Hynix prioritizing HBM4 ramp; analysts forecast 2027 mix at 55% HBM4 / 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 absorbing HBM3E demand from Q3.</cite> <cite index="8-11">Some analysts suggest HBM prices could enter correction post-2026 due to competition and expanded capacity, though dominant view is short-term shift unlikely given technical gaps.</cite> Structural tension: HBM capacity expansion (Samsung/Hynix $590B announcement) versus 2-3 year ramp cycle and locked hyperscaler LTAs through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix pledge $590B in Korea chip mega-cluster; shares fall 4-5% on cycle-peak fears
news_pulse.implication: Combined 911 trillion won investment (800 trillion won southwest cluster + accelerated Yongin fabs) signals all-in bet on sustained AI memory demand through late 2020s. Investor pushback on timing: 2-3 year fab lead times create classic late-cycle overcapacity risk if hyperscaler capex plateaus 2027-28. Near-term bullish (tight supply), long-term red flag (massive supply coming 2028-2029). Government goal to double Korea memory capacity in 5 years.

news_pulse.headline: Goldman raises Samsung 2027 HBM price growth forecast from 14% to 44%; cites DDR5 spot strength
news_pulse.implication: Spot-to-contract spread (DDR5 +25%, DDR4 +45%) historically leads contract price adjustments. Goldman's 3x upward HBM revision and 'not the ceiling' language suggests buy-side under-earning HBM ASP trajectory into 2027. Positive for both Samsung and Hynix gross margins, but also validates extended supercycle thesis underpinning $590B capex bet.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers hit $700B in 2026 capex; Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta raises to $125-145B
news_pulse.implication: 77% YoY capex growth from big five (MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/META/ORCL) confirms AI infrastructure arms race intact. Meta's guidance raise and subsequent 9.25% stock drop signals market concern over ROI timing—directly relevant to memory demand sustainability. Sequoia's $600B revenue-vs-capex gap widening in 2026. Bullish near-term for HBM/DDR5 volume, but capex fatigue narrative building.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrows to ~10% by end-2026 from 20%; capacity 120-140K wpm
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS easing through 2H26 removes key AI accelerator bottleneck, enabling faster GPU/ASIC shipments and therefore HBM attach. TSMC May symposium guided >80% CAGR 2022-2027 for CoWoS. Nvidia locked 60% of 2025-26 capacity. Positive for Hynix (Nvidia primary supplier) and Samsung (Broadcom/Google TPU ramp). Watch for OSAT share gains (ASE, Amkor) as TSMC outsources simpler RDL products.

news_pulse.headline: Mizuho lifts TSMC CoWoS forecast to 140K/month in 2026, 190-200K in 2027 on Nvidia Vera CPU demand
news_pulse.implication: 12-hour-old upgrade; Mizuho raising CoWoS estimates for Nvidia Vera CPU (Arm-based server) and Rubin GPU. Incremental positive for HBM content per server—CPUs increasingly using HBM/LPDDR in AI inference configs. Confirms packaging no longer gating factor by 2H26, shifting focus back to memory supply as next constraint.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q2 2026 DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75%; server LTAs locking in floors
news_pulse.implication: Sequential price growth decelerating from Q1's 90-95% DRAM jump but still extreme by historical standards. NAND accelerating faster than DRAM for first time this cycle (enterprise SSD demand). CSP long-term agreements with floor pricing reduce downside risk for Samsung/Hynix but also cap spot-driven upside. TrendForce April bulletin noted server DDR5 profitability overtaking HBM—margin mix shift to watch.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 spot price ($2.10/Gbit) now exceeds HBM3e contract ($1.70/Gbit) per Counterpoint
news_pulse.implication: Legacy DRAM inversion reflects big-three (Samsung/Hynix/Micron) EOL of DDR4/LPDDR4X, driving extreme scarcity. Taiwanese second-tier (Nanya, Winbond) benefiting but lack capacity to fill gap. Reinforces HBM/DDR5 capacity reallocation is structural, not cyclical. Spot buyers (SMB OEMs, distributors) facing acute pain; hyperscalers insulated via LTAs. Memory now strategic allocation item, not commodity.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix 2025 revenue 97.15T won (+46.76% YoY), earnings 42.92T won (+116.89%); analysts 'Strong Buy'
news_pulse.implication: FY2025 results confirm margin leverage from HBM/DDR5 mix shift. 37 analysts average 12-month target implies +20% upside from current. Earnings growth (+117%) outpacing revenue (+47%) validates pricing power thesis. 2026 guidance will be critical: if revenue growth decelerates despite pricing strength, signals volume constraints (CoWoS, internal capacity) becoming binding.

brief.derivatives_signal: No price data in payload; unable to assess ADR premium/discount or options flow. Macro context: KOSPI up 95% YTD per KED Global, extreme outperformance driven by memory supercycle. Samsung and Hynix shares both fell 4-5% on Monday 6/29 despite $590B announcement—classic 'sell the news' on long-duration capex with 2-3 year payback. If ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) underperform local shares, signals foreign institutional caution on cycle timing. Watch for put skew expansion in Hynix as purer memory play with higher beta to any AI capex slowdown headlines.

TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price updates for July 1—DDR5 spot premium widening would validate Goldman's HBM upward revision thesis
Any Samsung or Hynix commentary clarifying $590B investment timeline and HBM4 qualification milestones—market needs more granularity on 2027-2028 capacity additions
